C1.sentence: At the landing revision corpus/evidence/round91/control-driver-r91.py verify --root . --repo . --rev F --receipts-rev C prints CONTROL_DRIVER_R91=PASS (exit 0) with COMMITTED_OK=6/6 EXACT_OK=6/6 PIN_OK=6/6 FRESH_OK=6/6 over the six committed receipts of controls/expected.tsv; every required header key (case, expected_exit, exit, computed_against) appears exactly once and carries the row's value; # computed_against= equals --rev; every required K=V equals one whole body token and every K>=N predicate holds; the first file each row's command names as its script, and the expectations file, is pinned in instrument-pins.txt with the on-disk bytes and the blob at --rev hashing to the pin; SELF_PIN prints rev and receipts_rev; a .txt file that parses as a receipt and that no expected row scores is UNSCORED_RECEIPT; and control-forgeries-r91.py prints FORGERY_REFUSED=6/6 PRIOR_ACCEPTED=6/6 POSITIVE=pass.

kill_rules.K1: predicate not met at the landing revision
kill_rules.K2: a forgery accepted by r91, the positive refused, or r90 refuses a forgery
kill_rules.K3: a genuine row moved or the verification path wrote the receipts directory
kill_rules.K4: the pass skips the work: missing receipt accepted, committed receipt not read, substring token match, or the pin minted in verify

named_limits: a coherent joint edit of instrument, pin, receipt and expectation row survives (that edit is the harness)
whole-token matching binds one field per token, not its semantic role
the pin names the script a row's command mentions first; a second unpinned script is not seen
the self-pin detects a moved byte inside a named commit, not a rewritten history
the driver cannot see a pinned script that reads data outside its own bytes
